items.title: Reclassify cable theft through targeted legal and enforcement reforms
items.summary: LETTERS: The NST special report on increasingly sophisticated and dangerous copper and cable theft is deeply concerning, not only from an operational standpoint but, more importantly, from a public safety perspective. Any interference with rail signalling, power supply, or control systems introduces risks that extend far beyond inconvenience — they place passengers, frontline workers, and the wider public in harm's way. Cable theft in the rail sector should no longer be viewed as a simple property crime.

items.title: KFC picks Coca-Cola as US soda supplier, ditches longtime partner PepsiCo
items.summary: LOUISVILLE, (United States): Fast-food chain KFC on Thursday signed Coca-Cola as its beverage partner for US stores, bringing to a close a relationship with PepsiCo that dates back about four decades. While PepsiCo later spun off KFC in 1997, it continued to be a beverage partner for its parent Yum Brands. Yum Brands and PepsiCo just renewed agreements across Taco Bell and KFC International stores, a spokesperson for PepsiCo told Reuters.

items.title: Bring back caning? Dewan Rakyat debate heats up as MPs push tougher discipline and anti‑bullying reforms
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 16 — Issues related to education, including aspects of student discipline and safety, teaching quality, and the empowerment of skills education, took centre stage at the conclusion of the first week of the policy-level debate on the Supply Bill 2027 in the Dewan Rakyat yesterday. Lim Guan Eng (PH-Bagan) during his debate suggested caning be reinstated in schools as one of the measures to address discipline and bullying issues, along with regular psychological evaluations for teachers assigned to carry out the punishment. Touching on skills education, Datuk Dr Richard Rapu @ Aman Begri (GPS-Betong) urged the government to expand access to Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) for rural youth, especially in Sarawak, with training programmes aligned to the actual needs of the industry and job market.

items.title: Police record 199 criminal cases involving Rohingya
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Police recorded 199 criminal cases involving Rohingya refugees in the country between 2022 and August 2026. Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said Selangor recorded the highest number of cases at 58, followed by Kedah with 26 and Kuala Lumpur with 22. Saifuddin said National Security Council (NSC) Directive No.

items.title: JPJ officer dies after lorry crashes into department vehicle during inspection
items.summary: SEREMBAN, Oct 16 — A Road Transport Department (JPJ) officer was killed and another seriously injured in a crash involving a JPJ vehicle and two lorries on the North-South Expressway southbound near the Senawang exit last night, Sinar Harian reported. A second lorry travelling behind them is believed to have lost control before crashing into the JPJ sport utility vehicle (SUV) and the lorry being inspected. However, a senior Negeri Sembilan JPJ officer confirmed that one of the department’s personnel had died in the crash.

items.title: Swimming coach held after police seize RM6.8m in drugs in Melaka, Johor
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 16 — A 27-year-old swimming coach has been arrested on suspicion of drug trafficking after police seized drugs worth RM6.8 million in two raids in Melaka and Johor, Berita Harian reported. Jasin district police chief Superintendent Lee Robert said the suspect was detained at the Lipat Kajang toll area at about 11.30am on Wednesday during a roadblock conducted by the district police headquarters’ traffic investigation and enforcement division and narcotics crime investigation division. Lee reportedly said that preliminary investigations and information obtained from the suspect led police to conduct a follow-up operation in Johor with the state’s narcotics crime investigation department.

items.title: Mohamad Hasan says diplomacy first in haze crisis, warns enforcement risks severing Indonesia ties
items.summary: SEREMBAN, Oct 16 — Malaysia will continue to use diplomatic channels and Asean mechanisms to address the transboundary haze issue with Indonesia through a phased approach that prioritises its people’s interests and health, without jeopardising bilateral relations, said Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan. He said discussions between leaders and regional channels are the preferred approaches to addressing sensitive issues involving neighbouring countries, rather than legal enforcement measures or the issuance of diplomatic notes. In a related development, Mohamad said Malaysia will submit a non-paper at the upcoming Asean Senior Officials’ Meeting and Asean Foreign Ministers’ Meeting as part of efforts to strengthen regional mechanisms to address transboundary haze.

items.title: Oil prices edge down as investors weigh possible US sanctions on 'shadow fleet'
items.summary: BEIJING: Oil prices edged down on Friday morning as investors weighed risks in the Middle East and possible US moves to ease restrictions on the world's "shadow fleet" of tankers. Brent crude futures fell 41 US cents, or 0.39 per cent, to US$105.51 a barrel by 0012 GMT, while US West Texas Intermediate crude futures fell 54 US cents, or 0.55 per cent, to US$97.43. WTI settled more than three per cent higher on Thursday after a large drawdown in US crude stocks supported prices, while Brent crude was little changed.

items.title: Trump scraps plan to livestream execution after fierce backlash
items.summary: WASHINGTON: US President Donald Trump on Thursday canceled plans to livestream the firing squad execution of a convicted military base mass shooter, reversing a widely condemned move by Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth. The plan to make Nidal Hasan's execution public was opposed at home and abroad, with US Democratic and Republican politicians, the Catholic Church and the United Nations all expressing outrage. Pentagon spokesman Sean Parnell said Hegseth and Trump had spoken before the announcement.

items.title: Customs officer murdered at KLIA quarters as husband surrenders, police launch full investigation
items.summary: Negeri Sembilan police chief Datuk Alzafny Ahmad confirmed that the police received information regarding the incident at approximately 8.30pm. The suspect also surrendered himself at a police station following the incident,” he said when contacted by reporters here yesterday. He said that the police are currently conducting a detailed investigation at the scene to determine the actual motive behind the murder, as well as the precise time the incident occurred.

items.title: MSCI set to remove Indonesia from global indexes
items.summary: JAKARTA: Indonesia's stock market is no longer worthy of "emerging market" status, according to MSCI, which intends to remove it from a suite of products tracked by global investors, in a major setback likely to trigger capital outflows. "Significant concerns remain around market dysfunction," MSCI said in a statement posted on its website. "Accordingly, MSCI considers Indonesia's continued classification as an emerging market no longer appropriate," it said.

items.title: Customs officer murder: 'The way she died is heartbreaking,' says grieving brother
items.summary: Her brother, Amran Ibrahim, 59, said the family was struggling to come to terms with the incident, which happened about 7pm yesterday at the Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) quarters in Jalan Kuarters KLIA here. Amran said he received a call from his younger brother about 7.30pm informing him that their youngest sister, Norhazwani Ibrahim, had allegedly been killed by her husband. I immediately contacted the police station because the suspect had also said he wanted to turn himself in," he said.

items.title: Shooter killed at Oregon elementary school; CNN, CBS report four dead in violence
items.summary: OREGON: A person with a gun opened fire on Thursday at an elementary school in Bend, Oregon, wounding multiple victims, including children, before the assailant was killed, possibly by an armed onlooker, according to police. Police in Bend, a city of about 100,000 residents in rural central Oregon, 175 miles (280 km) southeast of Portland, said the first call they received from the 1 p.m. (2000 GMT) incident "indicated that an unknown man had shot into a car" at Silver Rail Elementary School. Moments later, emergency dispatchers received multiple calls "reporting that a person had entered the school and begun shooting," police said in a statement.

items.title: Listening to understand, not simply to answer
items.summary: Yet, amid all this emphasis on speaking, we sometimes overlook one of the most important aspects of communication: listening. More importantly, we forget that there is a fundamental difference between listening to understand and listening simply to answer. Listening to understand requires a different mindset.

items.title: Q3 2027 GDP to moderate, as consumer remains cautious
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's economic growth is expected to moderate in the third quarter of 2026 as resilient exports and investment help offset cautious consumer spending amid rising costs, economists said. The economy expanded six per cent year-on-year in the second quarter, following 5.4 per cent growth in the first quarter, bringing first-half growth to 5.7 per cent. Exports rose 45.5 per cent year-on-year to RM191.1 billion in August, driven by a 66.5 per cent increase in electrical and electronics products amid strong demand for semiconductors and artificial intelligence-related equipment.

items.title: Ringgit opens flat against US dollar as markets assess US interest rate outlook
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The ringgit opened flat against the US dollar on Friday as expectations of restrictive US monetary policy offset support from a weaker greenback. At 8am, the ringgit was almost unchanged at 4.0800/0845 against the US dollar, compared with Thursday's close of 4.0800/0835. However, persistent US inflationary pressures and expectations that the US Federal Reserve (Fed) would maintain its restrictive monetary policy could temper the ringgit's gains.

items.title: Singapore exports rise 68.4pct in September
items.summary: SINGAPORE: Singapore's non-oil domestic exports rose 68.4 per cent year-on-year in September, marking the sixth consecutive month of growth above 20 per cent, according to government data. Electronics exports surged 107.6 per cent year-on-year in September, while non-electronic exports rose 54.2 per cent, Enterprise Singapore said in a statement. Exports to nine of Singapore's top 10 markets increased, with shipments to Hong Kong surging 112.1 per cent.

items.title: Pas to prioritise Umno, BN in GE16 negotiations
items.summary: ARAU: Pas will prioritise Umno and Barisan Nasional over other political parties in any negotiations for the next general election (GE16). "Whoever Pas chooses to cooperate with, Umno must not be left behind. "The unity between Pas and Umno must be preserved, and they must be prioritised in negotiations," he said when met yesterday.

items.title: Haze: Johor worst hit as Pasir Gudang records very unhealthy API of 203
items.summary: Another 23 air quality monitoring stations nationwide also recorded unhealthy readings. Putrajaya recorded a reading of 173. Another 37 air quality monitoring stations recorded moderate API readings, while none recorded good air quality.

items.title: MRT Kajang Line trains slower this morning after attempted cable theft
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Mass Rapid Transit (MRT) Kajang Line services experienced delays this morning following an attempted cable theft and trespassing on the tracks. Rapid KL said the delays affected services between Phileo Damansara and Pusat Bandar Damansara stations. Rapid KL also apologised for the inconvenience caused to passengers.

items.title: Venezuela's Maduro, wife plead not guilty to new US torture charges
items.summary: NEW YORK: Ousted Venezuelan president Nicolas Maduro and his wife Cilia Flores pleaded not guilty Thursday to new torture charges brought against the pair held in US custody since their extraordinary capture in January. They appeared at a New York court after prosecutors alleged they conspired to commit acts including waterboardings, rapes and beatings against victims, including American citizens, in Venezuelan detention. Since Maduro's capture, his vice president, Delcy Rodriguez, has governed Venezuela as interim leader under intense pressure from US President Donald Trump's administration.

items.title: Experts urge clear rules for seizing assets of drunk drivers [WATCH]
items.summary: Universiti Putra Malaysia Road Safety Research Centre head Associate Professor Dr Law Teik Hua such procedures must also protect third parties and allow offenders to challenge seizures they considered excessive. He said judicial discretion would also be necessary to assess offenders' actual financial circumstances and distinguish genuine hardship from attempts to evade payment. Loke said the measures were intended to ensure compensation orders under amendments to the Road Transport Act provided meaningful recourse, particularly when offenders claimed they could not afford to pay.

items.title: Budget 2027: How much tax could Malaysians save under the proposed new rates? We did the maths for you
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 16 — How much will you be able to save in taxes in Malaysia, based on the proposed new income tax rates and individual tax relief in Budget 2027? Since Malaysia uses a progressive tax system, the tax you have to pay will be based on the different tax rates for the different income bands in your overall chargeable income, instead of one flat tax rate for your entire chargeable income. So based on the proposed new tax rates for 2027, you could save RM300 or RM800 in tax, if your chargeable income is for example RM100,000 or RM150,000.

items.title: Singapore weighs action against companies link to transboundary haze, says PM Wong
items.summary: SINGAPORE: Singapore is looking into companies that may be responsible for forest fires in Indonesia, which have worsened haze conditions in the region, Prime Minister Lawrence Wong said. He said the government would take action under the Singapore's Transboundary Haze Pollution Act where warranted, while exploring the possibility of joint action with other countries. "The haze stems from forest and peatland fires in Indonesia, made worse by the extended dry period.

items.title: Cops step up K9 patrols at KLIA
items.summary: SEPANG: Police have stepped up K9 unit patrols at Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA), particularly during peak hours, following several recent security incidents. KLIA police chief Assistant Commissioner M. Ravi said the patrols, previously conducted periodically, had been increased to bolster security at the airport. He said deployments were planned around peak periods.

items.title: 'Great to be back!' Harry, Meghan in first joint outing since UK return
items.summary: NOTTINGHAM, United Kingdom: Britain's Prince Harry and his wife on Thursday carried out their first joint engagement since their surprise move back to the UK in August, with Meghan telling wellwishers: "It's great to be back." King Charles III's 42-year-old younger son and Meghan, 45 – who left Britain and quit royal duties in 2020 amid a bitter royal family feud – were greeted with cheers as they arrived in the central English city of Nottingham. Known formally as the Duke and Duchess of Sussex, the last time Harry and Meghan appeared together at a public event in Britain was when they attended the late Queen Elizabeth II's funeral in September 2022.

items.title: Cheaper essentials for military personnel, veterans at Pernama
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Military personnel and veterans will be able to buy essential goods at discounted prices throughout the year under a Defence Ministry initiative offered through Malaysian Armed Forces Trading Corporation (Pernama) outlets. Khaled said Pernama must channel its profits back to the armed forces by offering cheaper goods. "But for that to happen, military personnel must support Pernama.

items.title: Ambani's Jio seeks US$3.2b in record India IPO
items.summary: MUMBAI: India's Jio Platforms Ltd, the digital arm of conglomerate Reliance Industries Ltd, is aiming to raise more than US$3 billion in what would be the country's biggest-ever initial public offering (IPO), after announcing pricing details ahead of next week's launch. A sale at the top end of the range would raise around US$3.2 billion, surpassing the previous national IPO record of US$2.9 billion set by Hyundai Motor India Ltd in 2024. While Jio has expanded into areas ranging from artificial intelligence to enterprise network services, it is best known for telecommunications subsidiary Reliance Jio Infocomm Ltd, India's largest mobile operator by subscribers.

items.title: Mexico gives social networks one month to remove violent content
items.summary: MEXICO CITY: Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum on Wednesday ordered Meta, TikTok, X, Apple and Microsoft to remove content inciting violence on their social networks following a spate of deadly attacks in schools. In the past two weeks, two people have been killed and several others have been injured in two separate school attacks. Sheinbaum linked the violence to "behaviour associated with communication on social media".

items.title: Police confirm Customs officer murdered by husband at KLIA quarters
items.summary: Negri Sembilan police chief Datuk Alzafny Ahmad confirmed that the police received information regarding the incident around 8.30 pm. The suspect also surrendered himself at a police station following the incident," he said when contacted by reporters. He said police are currently conducting a detailed investigation at the scene to determine the motive behind the murder, as well as the exact time the incident occurred.

items.title: Tuition teacher held over sexual assault, unnatural sex involving five boys
items.summary: City police chief Datuk Fadil Marsus said the offences took place at the suspect's house, which was also used as a tuition centre. He said police had received five separate reports involving teenage and child victims, all lodged at the Bukit Jalil police station. Fadil said police had conducted detailed investigations and recorded statements from various parties.

items.title: Student raises questions over donations to Najib
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A student representative has questioned public donations to former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak, raising concerns over fundraising efforts for a leader convicted in the SRC International case. Ummi Umairah Bakhit of Universiti Malaya raised the issue during a dialogue with former minister Khairy Jamaluddin, Selangor Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari and Johor Menteri Besar Datuk Onn Hafiz Ghazi at the World Trade Centre Kuala Lumpur. She expressed surprise at the public's willingness to contribute to Najib's fundraising campaign, citing the former prime minister's legal cases linked to 1Malaysia Development Bhd (1MDB).

items.title: Student leader raises corruption concerns with MBs, Khairy
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A Universiti Malaya student representative today sought the views of two menteris besar and a former health minister on corruption, asking how political leaders should address allegations of wrongdoing and encourage young Malaysians to speak up. She cited reports of alleged corruption involving political figures, including allegations that the son of a political figure had received RM4 million without working. In response, Khairy said corruption should be discussed openly, regardless of whether political leaders were involved, and urged the public to take a principled stand against wrongdoing.

items.title: Indonesia tests dry ice to disperse haze in South Sumatra
items.summary: JAKARTA: Indonesia has begun testing the use of dry ice to disperse thick haze caused by forest fires in South Sumatra, deploying 1,600kg in an experimental weather modification operation yesterday. National Disaster Management Agency (BNPB) Disaster Data, Information and Communication Centre acting head Berton Panjaitan said the operation involved two flights, each carrying 800kg of dry ice, targeting areas around Sultan Mahmud Badaruddin II International Airport in Palembang. South Sumatra is among Indonesia's six priority provinces for forest and land fire suppression, alongside Riau, Jambi, West Kalimantan, Central Kalimantan and South Kalimantan.

items.title: Pilgrims caught up in Houthi strikes on Saudi Arabia
items.summary: PILGRIMS in Saudi Arabia may not have anticipated being caught up in an air war, but some experienced an attack by Yemen's Houthis first-hand and others have been forced to change their plans. Saudi media reported that a Bangladeshi imam leading a group of dozens of pilgrims was killed and others wounded in the attack. Although most international pilgrims fly directly into Madinah or Jeddah airports, many others travel via Saudi Arabia's other main air hubs, including the many pilgrims who already live in the kingdom.

items.title: [UPDATED] Husband surrenders after wife found murdered at KLIA quarters
items.summary: NILAI: A 35-year-old civil servant was found murdered at a government quarters unit along Jalan Kuarters KLIA, with her husband identified as the suspect. Negri Sembilan police chief Datuk Alzafny Ahmad said police received information on the incident around 8.30pm before a team was dispatched to the scene. "We received initial information that a 35-year-old female civil servant had been murdered.

items.title: PM Anwar vows to fast‑track UM hostel project, says no leakages or wastage allowed
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 15 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim wants the Universiti Malaya (UM) Student Residence project to serve as a model for development management that is clean, efficient, and free from leakages or the wastage of public funds. He said the implementation of this project must draw lessons from the shortcomings of past project management which led to cost overruns, delays, and abandoned construction sites ultimately resulting in losses for the nation. Therefore, vice-chancellor, ensure that UM and this Student Residence project become an example for other agencies to emulate.

items.title: MOE reverts to haze plan: Schools shut at API 200, outdoor classes at 100, parents may keep kids home
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 15 — The Ministry of Education (MOE) has reverted to the National Haze Action Plan (PTJK) guidelines, which mandate the immediate closure of schools when the Air Pollutant Index (API) reaches 200, following input from various relevant agencies. Education Minister Fadhlina Sidek said that under the PTJK, all outdoor classroom activities must also be halted when the API exceeds 100. “In managing the haze, specific actions must be taken for each API reading level.

items.title: Conference of Rulers deliberates PM term limits, AG‑PP separation and Child Act amendments
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 15 — The proposed constitutional amendments to limit the Prime Minister’s tenure and separate the roles of the Attorney-General and Public Prosecutor were among the key matters discussed at the 273rd Conference of Rulers meeting at Istana Negara. The two-day meeting, which began yesterday, was chaired by the Sultan of Perak, Sultan Nazrin Shah. His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, attended the second day’s proceedings, accompanied by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.

items.title: Selangor schools in Klang, Petaling, Gombak and more closed tomorrow as haze worsens
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Oct 15 — Schools under the Klang, Kuala Selangor, Kuala Langat, Hulu Langat, Gombak, Sepang, Petaling Perdana and Petaling Utama district education offices will be closed tomorrow due to the haze. However, the Selangor State Education Department (JPNS) said in a statement today that schools under the Hulu Selangor and Sabak Bernam district education offices will operate as usual. “Parents, guardians, students and the wider education community are advised to take note of this announcement and refer to JPNS channels for the latest updates,” the statement said.

items.title: Sudden death probe opened after student’s fatal fall at Penang dormitory
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Oct 15 — A female university student died after allegedly falling from a building in the hostel block of a higher education institute in Jalan Bukit Gambir, Gelugor here today. Timur Laut district police chief ACP Abdul Rozak Muhammad said the police received a phone call from the university at 8.40am informing them of the discovery of the body of a 21-year-old female student residing in the dormitory. The student’s body was found at 7.25am by the university’s cleaning staff.

items.title: Penang statutory body chief pleads not guilty to 15 graft charges totalling RM800,000
items.summary: Datuk Dr Shaik Hussein Mydin, 53, is accused of corruptly receiving RM847,107.61 through Aliran Ilham Sdn Bhd (AISB) in multiple transactions from ATSH Management Sdn Bhd (ATSH) director Datuk R. Albert Suresh. Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) deputy public prosecutors Lim Jin Hong and Nurnajihatul Idayu Mohd Azuyar proposed bail of RM1 million, with additional conditions requiring the accused to surrender his passport, report to the MACC office monthly and refrain from interfering with prosecution witnesses. Shaik Hussein was represented by a seven-member legal team led by Datuk Amer Hamzah Arshad, comprising Datuk Hasnal Rezua Merican, Mohd Shahrullah Khan, Simon Tan, Dr Shamsher Singh Thind, Muzzammil Merican and Intan Nur Alia Nodzri.

items.title: Court of Appeal upholds 30‑year jail, 12 strokes for trader who hid step‑brother’s body in cement drum
items.summary: A three-judge panel comprising Justices Datuk Noorin Badaruddin, Datuk Meor Hashimi Abdul Hamid and Datuk Seri Latifah Mohd Tahar unanimously dismissed Mohamad Zamhuri Azami’s appeal against his conviction and sentence. The panel also dismissed the prosecution’s appeal to impose the death penalty on the 31-year-old accused. Delivering the court’s unanimous decision, Justice Noorin said the sentence imposed by the High Court was appropriate and did not warrant appellate intervention.

items.title: Malaysia’s haze map turns red: Klang, Nilai, Shah Alam among worst affected at near‑200 API
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 15 — A total of 34 areas recorded unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings as of 5pm today, with Klang, Selangor recording the highest reading at 195. A total of 34 areas nationwide recorded moderate API readings, while no areas recorded good air quality. API readings between zero and 50 indicate good air quality, 51 to 100 indicate moderate air quality, 101 to 200 indicate unhealthy air quality, 201 to 300 indicate very unhealthy air quality, while readings above 300 are classified as hazardous.

items.title: Dzulkefly: Families of MOH staff killed in Sarawak helicopter crash to receive pensions from Oct 21
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 15 — The next-of-kin of four Ministry of Health (MOH) staff who perished in a helicopter crash in Long Lellang, Ulu Baram, Sarawak, will begin receiving monthly derivative pension payments starting Oct 21. Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad said MOH, in collaboration with the Public Service Department (PSD) and the Sarawak State Health Department, has managed the disbursement of derivative pension benefits and appropriate financial assistance to the next-of-kin in a comprehensive and prudent manner. He noted that the total lump-sum payments for which the next-of-kin are eligible include compensation for accumulated leave (GCR), a derivative gratuity, funeral expense assistance, and an ex-gratia death payment.

items.title: Malaysia has done its best on haze talks with Indonesia, says PM Anwar
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 15 — The government has done its utmost to engage Indonesia in addressing the worsening transboundary haze, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said today. Anwar was responding to allegations that the government had not been proactive enough in tackling the transboundary haze issue. Yesterday, former Health Minister Khairy Jamaluddin criticised Malaysia for being “too soft” in its dealings with Indonesia over the haze, calling for a firmer stance.

items.title: KL police chief: Chemistry, pathology reports pending in custodial death case
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 15 — Police are awaiting the full report from the Chemistry Department and official pathology results to complete their investigation into the recent death of a man in police custody. Kuala Lumpur police chief Datuk Fadil Marsus said the cause of death of the local man, who was in his 40s, had yet to be determined pending the reports. He said the investigation was being conducted independently and thoroughly by the Bukit Aman Death in Custody Criminal Investigation Unit (USJKT), in collaboration with the Integrity and Standards Compliance Department (JIPS).

items.title: Woman brushing teeth behind wheel flashes middle finger before kicking auxiliary cop in groin at Glo Damansara
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 15 — A woman who was allegedly brushing her teeth behind the wheel flashed her middle finger at an auxiliary police officer before getting out of her car and kicking him in the groin during a bizarre confrontation at Glo Damansara yesterday. The woman then managed to escape after a struggle with the 30-year-old officer, leaving police hunting for her following the incident in Taman Tun Dr Ismail (TTDI). Brickfields district police chief ACP Hoo Chang Hook said the officer approached the car to reprimand the woman and instruct her to move her vehicle.

items.title: Selangor, Putrajaya, Negeri Sembilan, Pahang schools stay open tomorrow amid haze
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 15 — All educational institutions under the Ministry of Education (MOE) in Negeri Sembilan, Pahang, Selangor, and Putrajaya will operate as usual tomorrow. In separate statements today, the State Education Departments (JPN) in the three states and the Putrajaya Federal Territory Education Department (JPWPP) encouraged all pupils, teachers, support staff (AKP), and school personnel to wear face masks. In Negeri Sembilan, the JPN said all outdoor activities — including physical education, co-curricular and sports activities, camps, celebrations, assemblies, and open-hall events — must cease if the Air Pollutant Index (API) exceeds 100.

items.title: Honeymoon hiccup: Malaysian couple’s car triggers Bangkok bomb scare
items.summary: BANGKOK, Oct 15 — A Malaysian couple on their honeymoon in Thailand sparked a security alert in Bangkok on Wednesday after their car was found parked in a prohibited area, prompting authorities to call in an Explosive Ordnance Disposal (EOD) team to inspect the vehicle. Metropolitan Police Bureau Commissioner Pol Lt Gen Siam Boonsom said the Malaysian-registered red car was found parked on the pavement along Sukhumvit 17 Lane in Bangkok’s Lumpini district, raising concerns amid heightened security for the ongoing IMF-World Bank Group Annual Meetings 2026. He said Bangkok Metropolitan Administration (BMA) officials spotted the vehicle during a patrol on Wednesday afternoon and alerted the authorities over concerns that it might contain hazardous materials.

items.title: Selangor launches SA500 financing scheme for SMEs, NINE super app to consolidate services
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 15 — Selangor today launched a financing initiative for businesses facing cash flow constraints alongside a super app intended to bring government services, payments and mobility options onto a single digital platform. Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari said Selangor Advance 500 (SA500) would help eligible companies and contractors undertaking state-related projects manage their cash flow, while the NINE Super App would make government services and everyday transactions more accessible to the public. Amirudin said access to financing remained a challenge for many businesses, with SA500 intended to ease cash flow pressures and help eligible companies sustain their operations.

items.title: Seven seats in play, 21 firmly held: Zahid stakes out BN’s position in Melaka
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 15 — Barisan Nasional (BN) has said it will retain the 21 seats it won in the previous Melaka state election, leaving Perikatan Nasional’s (PN) component parties to negotiate over the remaining seven constituencies as discussions over electoral cooperation continue ahead of next month’s polls. BN chairman Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said the coalition was holding talks with PN’s core parties following the suspension of activities by the Opposition coalition, but made clear that BN had no intention of giving up the seats it currently holds. He said statements by PH leaders at both national and state levels indicated that the coalition had lost interest in working with BN for the Melaka election.

items.title: Pushing mega-projects, Hamzah Zainudin criticises Budget 2027 as ‘lacking vision’
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 12 — Opposition Leader Datuk Seri Hamzah Zainudin today criticised Budget 2027 as “lacking vision”, arguing that the federal government’s spending plan lacks a long-term economic plan and relies heavily on short-term handouts. Hamzah (PN-Larut) cited the government’s failure to meet its target of RM90 billion in development expenditure for two consecutive years, arguing this indicates poor fiscal management that could fuel concerns about potential under-investment in infrastructure projects. Anwar tabled a record RM459 billion federal spending plan for next year, of which some RM83 billion is earmarked for development.

items.title: Veterinary extension officers key to Malaysia’s food security, says deputy minister
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 15 — Veterinary extension officers play a crucial role in bridging government policies, the expertise of the Department of Veterinary Services (DVS) and the farming community to boost livestock productivity and strengthen national food security. Themed “Veterinary Extension: A Driver for Productivity and Food Security”, the convention was also attended by Veterinary Services Department director-general Datuk Dr Mohd Noor Hisham Mohd Haron. The categories included Best State Veterinary Service, Best District Veterinary Service, Best Livestock-Based Industry Development Project, Best Veterinary Extension Project, Best Veterinary Extension Project Poster, Best Veterinary Extension Project Video Presentation, Best Veterinary Extension Mentor/Officer and Best VetEC (Veterinary Extension Centre) Operation.

items.title: Budget 2027: RM130M boost for local film, music, and creative content
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 15 — The allocation of more than RM130 million under Budget 2027 for the local film, music and creative industries is a timely move to boost the sector’s contribution to economic growth and talent development. MyCreative Ventures said in a statement today that the government’s support would help industry players nurture their talents, create high-quality content and build more resilient and sustainable creative businesses. “In an industry increasingly shaped by technology, digital content and global competition, creativity must extend beyond producing works to generating greater economic value,” it said.

items.title: Kepong knife attack: Chinese student charged with stabbing ex-girlfriend and her brother
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 15 — A 20-year-old Chinese national university student pleaded not guilty at the Sessions Court here today to two charges of causing grievous hurt by stabbing his former girlfriend and her younger brother with a knife last month. Chen Jun is accused of causing grievous hurt to Leong Kai Ting, 21, and her younger brother, Leong Shun Jie, 18, by stabbing them both with a knife capable of causing death. Chen Jun appeared in court in a wheelchair.

items.title: Perikatan ‘almost 100pc’ certain of Melaka election alliance, but Takiyuddin keeps potential partners under wraps
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 15 — Perikatan Nasional (PN) is almost certain to forge an alliance with other political parties ahead of the Melaka state election, its secretary-general Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan said today, although he stopped short of revealing who its potential partners might be. Takiyuddin did not disclose which parties PN was negotiating with or whether the talks involved BN. He said discussions over seat allocations were already under way, both with potential allies and among PN’s own component parties.

items.title: Zetrix AI pledges cooperation as police, MACC probe unpaid RM314m collections
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 15 — Zetrix AI Bhd will fully cooperate with authorities in an ongoing joint investigation by the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) and the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC). The company was responding to a query from Bursa Malaysia Securities dated Oct 14 regarding a media report entitled "Police say six witnesses questioned in probe into MyEG, Zetrix AI” published by The Edge Malaysia on Oct 13. Zetrix AI said it would communicate any material developments through official announcements.

items.title: Court hears charges against former UKM director accused of RM3.12m contract abuse
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Oct 15 — A former director of an education centre at Universiti Kebangsaan Malaysia (UKM) pleaded not guilty at the Sessions Court here today to two charges of abusing his position to secure employment contracts worth RM3.12 million in 2022. Datuk Prof Muhammad Hussin, 64, a retiree, entered the plea after the charges were read out before Judge Datuk Mohd Nasir Nordin. According to the charges, Muhammad, a member of Koperasi Siswazah Bangi Berhad (KSBB), allegedly abused his position to secure two contracts worth RM1.2 million and RM1.92 million respectively to manage the Master of Education programme through UKM’s Faculty of Education.

items.title: Sarawak man finds RM1b in bank account, asks ChatGPT to count the zeros — only to discover it’s a glitch
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 15 — When a Sarawak clinic manager opened his banking app and discovered a mysterious 10-digit balance, he did what some people might do when faced with an eye-watering number: he asked ChatGPT. But for Wan Muhammad Fairus, 33, whose account should have contained less than RM1,000, his unexpected brush with billionaire status was over almost as quickly as it began. According to Berita Harian , the father of four from Samariang, Kuching, was in his bedroom preparing to make a banking transaction when he stumbled upon the extraordinary balance.
